title: Grade 10 Physics National Exam & Practice 2018 (9 Chapters Combined)
description: Comprehensive examination bank combining 9 chapters (100 questions). Official Ethiopian national curriculum.

questions.questionText: A car moves at speed of 80.0 km/hr for 1.0 hour to East then back to West in which it travels at speed of 60.0 km/hr for 2.0 hrs. What is the average velocity of the car during its motion?
questions.explanation:
Average velocity is total displacement divided by total time, not total distance divided by total time.

The eastward displacement is 80 km, while the westward displacement is 60 × 2 = 120 km.

Taking east as positive, total displacement = 80 - 120 = -40 km, meaning 40 km west.

Total time = 1 + 2 = 3 hours.

Average velocity = -40/3 ≈ -13.3 km/hr.

questions.questionText: The second condition of equilibrium states that the sum of all
options: torques acting on an object must be zero.
torques acting on an object must be non-zero constant.
forces acting on an object must be non-zero constant.
forces acting on an object must be zero.
questions.explanation:
For a rigid body to be in rotational equilibrium, the net torque about any point must be zero.

This condition is written as ∑τ = 0.

The first condition of equilibrium concerns the net force, while the second condition concerns the net torque.

questions.questionText: A weight of 1000 N suspended from an aluminum wire of length 2.5 m causes a 4.0 x 10⁻³ tensile strain on the wire. What is the change in length of the aluminum wire?
questions.explanation:
Tensile strain is defined as strain = ΔL/L₀.

Therefore, the change in length is ΔL = strain × L₀.

Substituting the values gives ΔL = (4.0 × 10⁻³)(2.5) = 0.010 m.

Since 0.010 m = 1 cm, the change in length is 1 cm.

questions.questionText:
An object of mass m = 12 kg supported by two strings is in equilibrium as shown in the figure below.

If the angle a string with tension T₁ makes from the horizontal is θ = 37°, what is the tension T₂ in the horizontal string?
questions.explanation:
For equilibrium in the vertical direction: T₁ sin(37°) = mg.

 Using g = 10 m/s², mg = 12 × 10 = 120 N. 

Since sin(37°) ≈ 0.6, T₁ = 120 / 0.6 = 200 N.

 For equilibrium in the horizontal direction: T₂ = T₁ cos(37°).

 Since cos(37°) ≈ 0.8, T₂ =

 200 × 0.8 = 160 N.

questions.questionText:
A circuit shown below consists of three resistors and two batteries.

The magnitude of current denoted by I₃ is
questions.explanation:
Kirchhoff's current law is first applied at the junction to relate the three branch currents.

Kirchhoff's voltage law is then applied around the two loops to obtain simultaneous equations for the unknown currents.

Using the polarity and circuit arrangement shown, solving these equations gives I₃ approximately equal to 0.45 A.

questions.questionText: During a charging process by induction, a positively charged rod is brought closed to a neutral metal sphere mounted on an insulated stand without touching it. Then, the metal sphere
options: gains some protons whenever it is grounded.
gains some electrons, whenever it is grounded.
loses some electrons, whenever it is grounded.
becomes positively charged, whenever it is grounded.
questions.explanation:
A positively charged rod attracts free electrons toward the nearby side of the neutral metal sphere.

When the sphere is grounded, electrons can flow from the Earth into the sphere because they are attracted by the positive rod.

Thus, the sphere gains electrons and becomes negatively charged after the grounding and separation process.

questions.questionText: A positively charged rod is brought near to a neutral electroscope A and a negatively charged rod is brought near to a neutral electroscope B. What will happen to the gold foils of the electroscopes? The gold foils of
options: electroscope A attract and that of B repels each other.
electroscope A repels and that of B attracts each other.
questions.explanation:
When a charged rod is brought near a neutral electroscope, charges inside the electroscope redistribute by electrostatic induction.

For the positively charged rod, electrons are attracted toward the upper part, leaving the gold leaves with positive charge.

For the negatively charged rod, electrons are repelled toward the leaves, making both leaves negatively charged.

In both electroscopes, the two leaves acquire charges of the same sign and therefore repel each other.

questions.questionText:
Four resistors are connected to give a single circuit as shown in the figure below.

Which of the following statement describes the combination of the resistors correctly?
options: R₁ and R₄ are combined in series.
R₂ and R₄ are combined in parallel.
R₁ and R₂ are combined in series.
R₅ and R₄ are combined in parallel.
questions.explanation: Looking at the parallel network inside the circuit, the branches containing R₄ and R₅ are connected across the same two common nodes, making R₅ and R₄ combined in parallel.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the difference between electric and magnetic fields? Electric field
options: is produced by a single magnetic pole, whereas magnetic field is produced by electric dipole.
begins on a negative charge and end on a positive charge, whereas magnetic field inside a bar magnet begins on a North pole and end on a South pole.
is the region around an uncharged object, whereas magnetic field is a region around stationary charged object.
is produced by a unit pole of charge, whereas magnetic field is produced by a dipole of the magnet.
questions.explanation: Electric fields originate from electric charges (monopoles), while magnetic fields are typically produced by magnetic dipoles since isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist.

questions.questionText: If the magnitude of magnetic field produced at a distance of 2 cm from a long straight current carrying wire is 1.2 T, then what is the magnitude of magnetic field at a distance of 3 cm from the wire?
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire is inversely proportional to the distance from the wire, so B ∝ 1/r.

Therefore, B₂ = B₁(r₁/r₂).

Substituting the values gives B₂ = 1.2 × (2/3) = 0.8 T.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the property of magnetic field lines?
options: Outside a bar magnets, magnetic field lines emerge from the south pole and enter to the north pole.
Magnetic field lines cross each other.
Magnetic field lines form closed loops.
Magnetic field lines are closer to each other in a region where the magnetic field is weaker.
questions.explanation:
Magnetic field lines always form continuous closed loops.

Outside a bar magnet, they travel from the north pole toward the south pole, while inside the magnet they return from south to north.

Magnetic field lines do not cross one another because crossing would imply two different field directions at the same point.

questions.questionText:
An electron moving at speed of 5.0 × 10⁷ m/s along the positive x-axis enters a uniform magnetic field of 1.5 T directed along the negative y-axis as shown in the figure below.

What is the magnetic force exerted on the electron at the moment it enters into the uniform magnetic field?
options: 8.0 x 10⁻¹² N, directed out of the page
1.2 x 10⁻¹¹ N, directed in to the page
1.2 x 10⁻¹¹ N, directed out of the page
8.0 x 10⁻¹² N, directed in to the page
questions.explanation:
The magnitude of the magnetic force is F = |q|vBsinθ.

The velocity and magnetic field are perpendicular, so θ = 90° and sin90° = 1.

Therefore, F = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)(5.0 × 10⁷)(1.5) = 1.2 × 10⁻¹¹ N.

Using the right-hand rule for a positive charge, v⃗ × B⃗ points out of the page.

Because an electron is negatively charged, the force direction is opposite, so it points into the page.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is correct about the magnetic field lines of a bar magnet or an electromagnet?
options: Since both a bar magnet and an electromagnet are permanent magnets; the patterns of the magnetic field lines are similar.
The density of the magnetic lines of an electromagnet is increased when the current through the conductor is increased.
The direction of the magnetic field lines of an electromagnet is the same regardless of the direction of the current through the conductor.
The magnetic field lines outside a bar magnet are directed from the South to North pole, but are in reverse direction for an electromagnet.
questions.explanation:
The strength of an electromagnet's magnetic field is directly proportional to the current passing through it. 

Increasing the electric current increases the field strength, which corresponds to a higher density of magnetic field lines.

questions.questionText: The circular face of a solenoid is placed in front of the north pole of a bar magnet. Which of the following actions does NOT induce an electromotive force (emf) in the solenoid?
options: Moving both the solenoid and the magnet with the same speed in opposite directions
Moving the solenoid towards the magnet
Moving both the solenoid and the magnet with the same speed in the same direction
Keeping the solenoid stationary while bringing the magnet closer to it
questions.explanation:
To induce an electromotive force (emf) via Faraday's law, there must be a change in magnetic flux through the solenoid, which requires relative motion between the solenoid and the magnet. 

Moving both the solenoid and the magnet with the same speed in the same direction means the distance and magnetic flux remain constant, so no emf is induced.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements describe about magnetic domains in a magnetic material? Magnetic domains are
options: orderly line up when the material is magnetized.
orderly line up in both magnetized and un magnetized materials.
orderly line up in unmagnetized material.
randomly distributed when the material is magnetized.
questions.explanation:
In an unmagnetized magnetic material, magnetic domains are randomly oriented.

 When magnetized, these domains align orderly in the direction of the external magnetic field.

questions.questionText: To form an image of a distant object, the refracting telescope uses
options: an objective convex lens to collect light and form an image which is magnified by the convex lens of the eyepiece.
convex mirror to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the convex lens of the eyepiece.
an objective concave lens to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the concave lens of the eyepiece.
convex mirror to collect light and forms an image which is magnified by the concave lens of the eyepiece.
questions.explanation:
A refracting telescope uses lenses rather than mirrors.

The objective is a convex lens with a long focal length and collects light from the distant object to form a real image.

The eyepiece is also a convex lens and acts as a magnifying glass to enlarge the image formed by the objective.

questions.questionText: Two plane mirrors inclined at an angle of 72° to each other. How many images are formed when an object is placed between them?
questions.explanation:
For two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ, when 360°/θ is an integer, the number of images is n = 360°/θ - 1.

Here, θ = 72°, so 360°/72° = 5.

Therefore, n = 5 - 1 = 4 images.

questions.questionText:
Suppose the figure shown below represents some portion of the electromagnetic spectrum.

Which one of the following is correct about the nature of the electromagnetic waves represented by X and Y?
options: Waves X have longer wavelength than waves Y.
Waves Y have higher speed than waves X.
Waves X and Y has the same frequency.
Waves X have higher frequency than waves Y.
questions.explanation:
The electromagnetic spectrum is arranged from longer wavelength and lower frequency to shorter wavelength and higher frequency.

Since X is located before infrared, it represents electromagnetic waves with longer wavelengths than the waves represented by Y, which is beyond ultraviolet.

All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in vacuum, so Y does not have a higher speed than X.

questions.questionText: A light ray passing from air to glass has an angle of incidence 37° with the normal. If the refractive index of the glass is 1.54, what is the angle of refraction of the light?
questions.explanation:
Snell's law states that n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂.

For air, n₁ ≈ 1, while for glass n₂ = 1.54 and θ₁ = 37°.

Therefore, sinθ₂ = sin37°/1.54 ≈ 0.6018/1.54 ≈ 0.39.

Thus, θ₂ = sin⁻¹(0.39).

questions.questionText: A string which is vibrating with a frequency of 6.0 Hz, produces a transverse wave of wavelength 80.0 cm. What is the speed of the waves along the string?
questions.explanation:
The speed of a wave is given by v = f × λ. 

Given frequency f = 6.0 Hz and wavelength λ = 80.0 cm = 0.80 m,

 the speed is v = 6.0 × 0.80 = 4.8 m/s.

questions.questionText: When diverging light rays from a source are incident upon a mirror the rays are reflected from the mirror and form an image which is either real or virtual. The image formed is
options: virtual when the actual reflected/refracted rays are crossing at a point.
real when the backward extensions of reflected/refracted rays are crossing at a point.
real when the light rays from the image can be focused on a screen.
virtual when the light rays from the image can be focused on a screen.
questions.explanation: A real image is formed by actual converging light rays and can be projected and focused onto a screen, whereas a virtual image is formed by the apparent divergence of light rays and cannot be focused on a screen.

questions.questionText:
A beam of monochromatic light strikes the shiny side of a horizontal plane mirror as shown in the figure below.

What is its angle of reflection θr?
questions.explanation:
The angle of incidence is measured between the incident ray and the normal (perpendicular) to the mirror surface.

 Since the mirror is horizontal, the angle between the mirror surface and the normal is 90°.

 Given that the angle between the incident ray and the mirror surface is 40°,

 the angle of incidence is 90° - 40° = 50°.

 By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection θ_r is equal to the angle of incidence, so θ_r = 50°.

questions.questionText: Which of the following quantities is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Force has both magnitude and direction, therefore it is a vector quantity.

questions.questionText: Which quantity represents rate of change of displacement?
questions.explanation: Velocity measures rate of change of displacement.

questions.questionText: Vectors along the same straight line are called:
questions.explanation: Collinear vectors lie along the same line.

questions.questionText: The y-component of a vector lies along:
questions.explanation: The y-component lies along the vertical axis.

questions.questionText: Vectors that lie in the same plane are called:
questions.explanation: Coplanar vectors exist in the same plane.

questions.questionText: Which of the following quantities is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Temperature has magnitude only and no direction, so it is a scalar quantity.

questions.questionText: A steel rod has a Young's modulus of 2.0 x 10¹¹ N/m². If it experiences a strain of 0.001, what is the stress in the rod?
questions.explanation:
Young's Modulus (Y) = Stress / Strain.
 Therefore, Stress = Y × Strain.
 Stress = (2.0 x 10¹¹ N/m²) × 0.001 = 
2.0 x 10⁸ N/m².

questions.questionText: A blue object under a green light will appear:
questions.explanation:
A blue object absorbs green light and reflects blue light.

 Since no blue light is available (only green light is incident), the object absorbs the green light and appears black (or very dark).

questions.questionText: If the number of turns in a solenoid is doubled while keeping the length and current constant, the magnetic field inside:
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field B in a solenoid is proportional to the number of turns per unit length (n = N / L). 
Doubling N doubles the field B.

questions.questionText: For an ideal transformer, the power input to the primary coil is **equal** to the power output from the secondary coil. This is an application of the law of:
questions.explanation: Ideal transformers are assumed to be 100 percent efficient, meaning they conserve energy: P input = P output.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a method of charging a body?
questions.explanation: Polarization redistributes charge but does not create net charge on a body.

questions.questionText: The operation of an electric motor is based on which principle?
options: Motor effect (force on a current-carrying conductor).
questions.explanation: An electric motor uses the motor effect, which is the force exerted on a current-carrying wire when it is placed in a magnetic field, to produce torque and rotation.

questions.questionText: If a 4 A current flows through a resistor of 5 Ω, what is the voltage across it?
Two resistors of 8 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in series across 24 V. What is the current in the circuit?
Which of the following is NOT an application of X-rays?
questions.explanation:
While X-rays are used in diagnosis, Gamma rays are more commonly used for deep-penetrating radiotherapy to treat cancer.

 X-rays are generally not used for sterilization.

questions.questionText: In a simple AC generator, the rotating coil is connected to the external circuit via:
questions.explanation: Slip rings maintain continuous contact and allow the AC current (which reverses direction every half cycle) to pass to the external circuit.

questions.questionText: When a charged object is brought near an electroscope without touching it, the leaves diverge due to:
questions.explanation: Electrons redistribute in the electroscope due to induction.

questions.questionText: A coil with 100 turns has a magnetic flux of 0.05 Weber passing through it. What is the total magnetic flux linkage (N Phi)?
questions.explanation:
Magnetic flux linkage is N times Phi.
 N Phi = 100 turns * 0.05 Wb = 5 Weber.

questions.questionText: Electric current is defined as:
questions.explanation: Current is the rate of flow of charge.

questions.questionText: The energy transfer mechanism that does not require a material medium and relies solely on electromagnetic waves is:
questions.explanation: Heat transfer by radiation (e.g., from the Sun) involves the emission and absorption of electromagnetic waves, primarily infrared, and can occur in a vacuum.

questions.questionText: The two main types of electrical energy generated and used are:
questions.explanation: The two main types of current are Direct Current (DC), where the charge flows in one direction, and Alternating Current (AC), where the current direction periodically reverses.

questions.questionText: Which method of charging can create a permanent charge on an object without direct contact?
questions.explanation: Induction can charge an object by bringing a charged object near it.

questions.questionText: Which region of the EM spectrum is primarily used in TV remote controls for signal transmission?
questions.explanation: Most consumer remote controls use short-range infrared (IR) radiation to transmit signals.

questions.questionText: To produce the maximum induced current in a coil by moving a bar magnet, the magnet should be moved:
options: Slowly toward or away from the coil.
Quickly toward or away from the coil.
Very slowly and kept stationary inside the coil.
questions.explanation:
Induced EMF is proportional to the **rate of change** of magnetic flux.

 Moving the magnet quickly increases this rate, maximizing the induced current.

questions.questionText: The concept that light sometimes behaves as a stream of particles (photons) and sometimes as a wave is known as:
questions.explanation:
Wave-particle duality states that all matter exhibits both wave and particle properties.

 For light, this means it has wavelike properties (diffraction, interference) and particle-like properties (photons, photoelectric effect).

questions.questionText: An ammeter measures:
questions.explanation: Ammeters measure the flow of current.

questions.questionText: The ability of light to pass through a material is called:
questions.explanation:
Transmission is the passage of electromagnetic waves through a medium.

 Materials that transmit light are transparent or translucent.

questions.questionText: Which scientist unified electricity and magnetism and predicted the existence of electromagnetic waves?
questions.explanation: James Clerk Maxwell formulated the theory of electromagnetism and predicted that oscillating electric and magnetic fields propagate through space as electromagnetic waves.

questions.questionText: Which EM wave is used in remote sensing and weather forecasting because it can pass through clouds and precipitation?
questions.explanation: Radar (Radio Detection and Ranging) systems use microwaves to detect weather patterns, as these waves can penetrate the atmosphere and clouds.

questions.questionText: The primary cause of the heat we receive from the Sun is:
questions.explanation: The majority of the Sun's energy reaching Earth is in the visible and infrared regions of the spectrum, which contributes to heating the Earth.

questions.questionText: 32. Which one of the following statements is correct about the resistance of a conducting wire? The resistance of the wire is
options: directly proportional to the square of its length.
directly proportional to the square of its cross-sectional area.
inversely proportional to its cross-sectional area.
questions.explanation: The resistance ($R$) of a conductor is given by the formula $R = \rho \frac{L}{A}$, where $\rho$ is resistivity, $L$ is length, and $A$ is the cross-sectional area. The formula shows that resistance is **inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area** ($R \propto 1/A$) and directly proportional to the length ($R \propto L$). .

questions.questionText: What is the physical quantity that links the electric and magnetic fields in Faraday's Law of Induction?
questions.explanation: Faraday's Law states that the induced EMF (electric effect) is proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux (magnetic effect).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT a property of magnetic field lines?
options: They are closest together where the magnetic field is strongest.
They originate at the North pole and terminate at the South pole inside the magnet.
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines go from North to South outside the magnet and from South to North **inside** the magnet, thus forming closed loops.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about satellite motion?
options: satellite moving closer to the Earth takes longer time to complete one revolution than a satellite farther from the Earth.
For two satellites moving around the Earth at equal orbital radius, a heavier satellite has larger speed than a lighter one.
For equal orbital radius, a satellite moving around the Earth has smaller speed than a satellite moving about Moon.
satellite closer to Earth is faster than a satellite farther from the Earth.
questions.explanation:
According to orbital mechanics, the orbital speed of a satellite is given by:- 

v = √(GM/r), where r is the distance from the center of the Earth.

 Therefore, a satellite closer to Earth (smaller r) moves faster than one farther away.

questions.questionText: If a coil is moved through a uniform magnetic field at a constant velocity, the induced EMF will be:
questions.explanation:
Induced EMF is proportional to the rate of change of flux. 
Moving the coil through a uniform field at a constant velocity means the magnetic flux through the coil is not changing (as long as it remains entirely within the field), so the induced EMF is zero.

questions.questionText: An object is placed 25.0 cm in front of a concave mirror having focal length of 10.0 cm. The magnification of the mirror is _________.
questions.explanation:
The image distance (v) is found using the mirror formula: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u. 

With f = -10.0 cm and u = -25.0 cm, 1/v = 1/(-10) - 1/(-25) = -1/10 + 1/25 = (-5 + 2)/50 = -3/50, so v = -50/3 cm.

 The magnification (M) is then M = -v/u = -(-50/3) / (-25) = -2/3 = -0.67. 

The magnitude is 0.67, which corresponds to option C.

questions.questionText: An electron moving North enters a magnetic field directed East. The magnetic force on the electron is directed:
questions.explanation:
Using the Right-Hand Palm Rule for a positive charge (or the three-finger rule), the force would be Upward.

 Since the electron is negatively charged, the force is in the opposite direction, which is Downward.

questions.questionText: According to the convention, a positive focal length (f) corresponds to which type of mirror or lens?
questions.explanation:
Converging optical components have positive focal lengths:
 Concave mirrors and Convex lenses.

questions.questionText: Which of the following colors of visible light has the lowest energy?
questions.explanation:
Energy is proportional to frequency (E is proportional to f). 

Red light has the lowest frequency (and longest wavelength) in the visible spectrum, meaning it has the lowest photon energy.

questions.questionText: A current of 0.5 A flows for 2 minutes. How much charge passes through the circuit?
Which application utilizes X-rays due to their ability to penetrate soft tissues but be absorbed by denser materials like bone?
questions.explanation: X-rays are widely used in medicine to take pictures of bones and teeth because of this differential absorption property.

questions.questionText: Which color of light has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Violet light (around 400 nm) has the shortest wavelength in the visible spectrum.

questions.questionText: Arrange the following in order of increasing wavelength: 1) Visible Light, 2) X-rays, 3) Microwaves.
questions.explanation: Increasing wavelength means decreasing frequency/energy. The order from shortest to longest wavelength is: X-rays, Visible Light, Microwaves (2, 1, 3).

questions.questionText: Which component in a DC motor periodically reverses the direction of the current in the coil?
questions.explanation: The commutator is a split ring device that reverses the direction of the current in the armature coil every half-turn, ensuring the torque is always in the same direction, hence continuous rotation.

questions.questionText: The energy of a single photon is directly proportional to its:
questions.explanation:
According to Planck's equation, E = h times f (Energy equals Planck's constant times frequency).

 Therefore, energy is directly proportional to frequency.

questions.questionText: The main component used in magnetic tape and hard drives for data storage is a:
questions.explanation: Data storage requires materials that can retain their magnetic state (magnetization) permanently, which are known as hard magnetic materials (high coercivity).

questions.questionText: If resistance increases while voltage remains constant, the current:
questions.explanation:
I = V/R; 
increasing R reduces current.

questions.questionText: Which type of electromagnetic wave is used to carry audio signals in a standard AM (Amplitude Modulation) radio broadcast?
questions.explanation: AM radio uses the long-wavelength radio wave portion of the spectrum.

questions.questionText: Which of the following properties is constant for all electromagnetic waves traveling in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: The speed of light (c) in a vacuum is a universal constant for all electromagnetic waves, regardless of their frequency or wavelength.

questions.questionText: In a transformer, why must the primary and secondary coils be wound on the same core?
options: To maximize the magnetic flux linkage between the coils.
questions.explanation: The common soft iron core ensures that nearly all the magnetic flux produced by the primary coil passes through the secondary coil, maximizing the induced EMF and efficiency.

questions.questionText: A satellite revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit of radius r = 4 * 10¹⁶m. The period of the satellite is ______.
questions.explanation:
The period T of a satellite in a circular orbit is given by:- 

T = 2π√(r³ / GM), 
where G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² and M = 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg (mass of Earth).

 Substituting r = 4 × 10¹⁶ m gives T ≈ 2.5 × 10¹⁹ s.

questions.questionText: For a given converging lens, where should an object be placed to obtain a real image of the same size as the object?
questions.explanation: Placing the object at twice the focal length (2F, which is C for a mirror equivalent) yields a real, inverted, and same-size image.

questions.questionText: The image formed by a convex lens is used as a magnifying glass when the object is placed:
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass works by creating a virtual, upright, and magnified image, which occurs when the object is placed closer to the lens than the focal point (between F and the lens).

questions.questionText: The electric utility grid in most countries uses AC power instead of DC power primarily because AC can:
options: Be easily stepped up and down using transformers.
questions.explanation: The ability of AC to be easily transformed is the key reason for its use, as it allows for high-voltage, low-loss transmission over long distances.

questions.questionText: Which device uses the principle of electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: A generator (dynamo) converts mechanical energy (motion) into electrical energy based on Faraday's Law of Induction.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum (c) to the speed of light in a medium (v) is defined as the:
questions.explanation:
The refractive index n = c / v.

 It is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced in a medium.

questions.questionText: A converging lens is also known as a:
questions.explanation: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and causes parallel light rays to converge (meet) at a single point (the focal point).

questions.questionText: The energy stored in a charged conductor is due to:
questions.explanation: Energy is stored as electric potential energy due to voltage.

questions.questionText: Which phenomenon causes white light to split into its constituent colors when passing through a prism?
questions.explanation: Dispersion is the phenomenon where the speed (and thus the refractive index) of a medium varies with the wavelength of light, causing different colors to refract at different angles.

questions.questionText: An EM wave travels from air (n=1.0) into glass (n=1.5). Which property of the wave remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: When a wave passes from one medium to another, its frequency (determined by the source) remains constant, while its speed and wavelength change.

questions.questionText: Which characteristic of a DC motor is NOT improved by increasing the number of loops on the armature coil?
options: The strength of the magnetic field.
questions.explanation:
The magnetic field B is produced by the permanent magnets or electromagnets (field coils).

 Increasing the number of loops in the armature (rotor) increases the torque, speed, and efficiency, but not the field B itself.

questions.questionText: The minimum distance between an object and its real image in a concave mirror is:
options: Zero only at the focal point.
questions.explanation: The minimum distance is zero, which occurs when the object is placed at the center of curvature (C or 2F), as the image is also formed exactly at C.

questions.questionText: If resistance increases with constant voltage, current will:
questions.explanation: From I = V/R, current decreases.

questions.questionText: The phenomenon of light that explains why a coin at the bottom of a container of water appears shallower than it really is, is:
questions.explanation:
Light rays from the coin bend away from the normal when leaving the water (denser medium) into the air (less dense medium).

 This refraction makes the apparent depth smaller than the real depth.

questions.questionText: If an object is placed at the center of curvature (C) of a concave mirror, the image is formed at:
questions.explanation: For a concave mirror, when the object distance is twice the focal length (at C), the image is also formed at C, is real, inverted, and the same size.

questions.questionText: If displacement-time graph is a straight line, motion is:
questions.explanation: Straight line in x–t graph means constant velocity.

questions.questionText: If a transformer has 100 turns in the primary coil and 500 turns in the secondary coil, and the primary voltage is 12 V, the secondary voltage will be:
questions.explanation:
The voltage ratio is Vp / Vs = Np / Ns.

 Vs = Vp * (Ns / Np) = 
12 V * (500 / 100) =
 12 V * 5 = 60 V.

questions.questionText: A light ray that passes through the center of curvature of a spherical mirror after reflection:
options: Travels parallel to the principal axis.
questions.explanation: A ray passing through the center of curvature (C) hits the mirror surface perpendicularly (along the normal) and thus is reflected back along the same path (retrace).

questions.questionText: The arrow head of a vector represents:
questions.explanation: The arrow head indicates the direction of the vector.

questions.questionText: Which statement is true regarding the propagation of EM waves in a vacuum?
options: The electric field component is stronger than the magnetic field component.
The magnetic field component is stronger than the electric field component.
The electric and magnetic fields oscillate with the same amplitude.
The electric and magnetic fields are always in phase.
questions.explanation: In an EM wave, the oscillating electric field and magnetic field are always in phase (reach their maximum and minimum values simultaneously).

questions.questionText: A charged particle moves in a circle of radius R in a uniform magnetic field. If the speed of the particle is doubled, the new radius of the circle will be:
questions.explanation:
The radius R of the circular path is proportional to the speed v (R = m v / q B).

 Doubling the speed v doubles the radius R.

questions.questionText: Which equation represents the first equation of motion?
questions.explanation: The first equation of motion is v = u + at.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following units is NOT a possible unit of electric field strength?
questions.explanation:
Electric field strength (E) is defined as force per unit charge: E = F/q. 

Its SI unit is Newton per Coulomb (N/C).

 It can also be expressed as potential difference per unit distance: E = V/d, so Volt per meter (V/m) and Joule/(Coulomb * meter) are valid. 

Joule/Coulomb alone is just Volt, which is not a unit of electric field strength.

questions.questionText: The first condition for equilibrium (ΣF = 0) ensures that the object has no:
questions.explanation:
The first condition, that the vector sum of all forces is zero, is a direct application of Newton's Second Law (F=ma).

 If ΣF=0, then the acceleration 'a' must be zero.
 This prevents any change in the object's linear motion.

questions.questionText: If two equal vectors act in opposite directions, their resultant is:
questions.explanation: Equal and opposite vectors cancel out.

questions.questionText: Oersted's experiment showed that an electric current produces:
questions.explanation: Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a current-carrying wire deflected a nearby magnetic compass, demonstrating that an electric current creates a magnetic field.

questions.questionText: Neutral objects can be attracted to a charged body due to:
questions.explanation: Induced charges in a neutral object create attraction.

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct regarding electric discharge?
options: Discharge is the movement of charges from high to low potential
questions.explanation: Electrical discharge occurs as charges move to neutralize potential differences.
